title: 11 Things Not To Do This Coming School Year https://smartclassroommanagement.com/2018/06/30/11-things-not-to-do-this-coming-school-year/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Michael Linsin applies the principle of via negativa—improving by subtraction rather than addition—to classroom management. He argues that bad teacher habits, more than any single strategy, are the primary cause of student misbehavior, quietly creating excitability, animosity, and disrespect without teachers realizing it. He offers a list of eleven common habits, framed as "reverse resolutions," that teachers should simply stop doing before the coming school year. These range from showing outward frustration and glaring or lecturing to rewarding for good behavior, talking too much, and being inconsistent. Linsin contends that avoiding these behaviors alone will make a class naturally better behaved, without requiring teachers to add anything new to their repertoire. He closes by framing the process as one of deliberate subtraction of the harmful and self-sabotaging, making room for good outcomes to emerge.
points: Via negativa—improvement by avoiding harmful habits rather than adding new strategies—is presented as especially effective for classroom management.
Eleven specific teacher behaviors are named as causes of misbehavior, including glaring, over-praising, inconsistency, and micromanaging.
Bad habits can create excitability, animosity, indifference, and disrespect without the teacher ever realizing it.
Avoiding the eleven habits requires no new effort—just forethought and a decision to stop reacting emotionally.
The approach reframes classroom improvement as subtraction of the harmful, allowing good behavior to surface on its own.
quotes: Via negativa is a method of improvement whereby one focuses not on what to do to become more proficient.
Because, you see, bad teacher habits are a primary cause of misbehavior.
They can actually create excitability, animosity, indifference, immaturity, and disrespect without you even realizing it.
Simply avoid doing the following and your new class will become naturally, almost effortlessly, better behaved.
It does take some forethought. It does take making a deliberate decision to no longer be pushed around by your emotions, by what feels right in the moment, or by what your colleagues are doing.
It does take subtracting the bad, the harmful, and the self-sabotaging.
All eleven reverse resolutions—which have been covered extensively on this website—will save you from the most common habits and mistakes that cause an excitable, ill-behaved class.
